question: A shopkeeper gains 30% after allowing a discount of 20% on the marked price of an article. Find his profit per cent if the articles are sold at a marked price allowing no discount.
solution:
**Given:-** Profit % = 30% , % discount = 20%

**To find:-** Profit % when articles sold at market price with no discount

**Formula used:- Selling price = Market price - % discount × market price, % profit = **(Selling price - Cost price)/(Cost price)times 100

**Calculations:-** Let the market price of the article be Rs. 100,

Selling price = 100 - 20% × 100

**Selling price(SP) = Rs. 80**

% Profit = 30%

By using the formula of % profit,

⇒(SP-CP)/(CP)times 100 = 30

⇒(80-CP)/(CP)=(3)/(10)

⇒Cost price**(CP)= Rs. (800)/(13)**

**Selling price when the articles will be sold at marked price = Rs. 100**

⇒% profit without discount = (New SP - CP)/(CP)times 100

⇒% profit without discount = (100-frac{800)/(13)}{(800)/(13)}times 100

⇒% profit without discount = (1300-800)/(800)times 100 = (500)/(800)times 100

⇒**% profit without discount = (500)/(8)**** = 62.5%**

 

**.·.The % profit when an article is sold at the marked price without discount is 62.5%**
